colors.description: Semantic color tokens for surfaces, text, borders and intent. Every token adapts to light and dark themes.
whenToUse: Reference semantic tokens such as --color-text or --color-primary in every style.
Pair fill tokens like --color-primary with their --color-text-on-* token.
Use the -subtle and -border tokens of a tone for tinted, low-emphasis surfaces.
whenNotToUse: Never reference raw palette steps (--gray-*, --brown-*) from components or pages.
Do not hardcode hex or rgb values, even for one-off tweaks: add a token instead.
accessibility: Every text and fill pairing is checked against WCAG 2.1 AA by contrast.test.ts in both themes.
Text tokens reach 4.5:1 on all surfaces; borders and focus rings reach 3:1.
Color is never the only signal: pair tone with an icon or a label.

typography.description: A compact type scale built on Inter, with tight heading tracking and relaxed body leading.
whenToUse: Use Heading for titles and Text for body copy instead of styling raw elements.
Keep body text at sm or md; reserve 2xl and above for page titles.
whenNotToUse: Do not skip heading levels to get a different size: pick the level, then set size.
Avoid long passages in muted text, it is meant for secondary details.
accessibility: Sizes use rem so text scales with the browser font size.
Line lengths stay readable when content is capped with the measure tokens.

spacing.description: A 4px-based spacing scale used for padding, gaps and layout rhythm.
whenToUse: Use space-1 to space-3 inside components and space-4 to space-6 between them.
Use Stack gaps instead of margins to space siblings.
whenNotToUse: Do not use pixel values or arbitrary rem values for spacing.
accessibility: Generous spacing between interactive targets reduces accidental activation.

radius.description: Corner radii that scale with the size of the element they round.
whenToUse: Use radius-sm for small controls, radius-md for buttons and inputs, radius-lg for cards and popovers.
Use radius-full for pills, avatars and switches.
whenNotToUse: Do not mix radii within one component; nested corners should get smaller, not larger.
accessibility: Radius is purely visual and carries no meaning on its own.

shadows.description: Layered elevation shadows that read in both themes, from subtle controls to dialogs.
whenToUse: Use shadow-xs on controls, shadow-md on raised cards, shadow-lg on popovers and shadow-xl on dialogs.
Combine a shadow with a border so edges stay visible in dark mode.
whenNotToUse: Do not stack several shadow tokens on one element or invent new ones inline.
accessibility: Shadows never replace borders for controls that need a visible boundary.

button.description: Triggers an action or event, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog.
whenToUse: Use primary for the single most important action in a view.
Use secondary or ghost for supporting actions next to a primary button.
Use danger only for destructive actions, ideally confirmed in a dialog.
Use isLoading while an async action runs instead of disabling the button.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a button to navigate to another page: use Link.
Avoid more than one primary button in the same group.
Do not write vague labels like “OK”; say what happens, like “Save changes”.
accessibility: Renders a native button, so Enter and Space activate it and it is focusable by default.
Icon-only buttons require aria-label, enforced by the types.
While loading the button sets aria-busy and aria-disabled but stays focusable.
Use aria-pressed for toggle buttons; the pressed style follows the attribute.

props.name: icon
props.description: Renders an icon-only button. Requires aria-label.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a spinner and ignores clicks.

props.name: isFullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to its container.

link.description: Navigates to another page inside the app or to an external site.
whenToUse: Use inline links inside running text.
Use standalone for links that stand on their own, like “View all”.
Pass href for external URLs; they open in a new tab with a visible icon.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a link to trigger an action that stays on the page: use Button.
Avoid “click here”; the link text should describe the destination.
accessibility: Internal links use React Router and render a native anchor.
External links announce “opens in new tab” to screen readers.
Inline links stay underlined so they are not identified by color alone.

props.name: href
props.description: External URL. Opens in a new tab.

menu.description: A button that opens a list of actions, like a context or overflow menu.
whenToUse: Use for secondary actions that do not fit in the main toolbar.
Use the danger tone for destructive items and place them last.
Set isChecked on every item to turn the menu into a single choice, like a sort order.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a menu to pick a value in a form: use Select.
Avoid menus with a single item; show the action directly.
accessibility: The trigger exposes aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.
Focus moves into the menu when it opens and returns to the trigger when it closes.
Disabled items stay in the list and are announced as unavailable.
Items with isChecked become menuitemradio items, and the menu opens on the checked one.

keyboard.description: Opens the menu, or moves between items.
Moves to the first or last item.
Closes the menu and focuses the trigger.
Closes the menu and moves on.
Moves to the next item that starts with the typed letters.

props.name: label
props.description: Trigger label, also used to name the menu.

props.name: items
props.description: Items, or sections of items with an optional label. Items can have a shortcut.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Renders an icon-only trigger with the label as its name.

props.name: align
props.description: Which edge of the trigger the menu aligns to.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

checkbox.description: Lets people turn a single option on or off, or pick several options from a list.
whenToUse: Use for independent options where any combination is valid.
Use isIndeterminate on a parent checkbox when only some children are checked.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for mutually exclusive choices: use RadioGroup.
For settings that apply immediately, prefer Switch.
accessibility: Wraps a native checkbox inside its label, so the whole label is clickable.
The hint is linked with aria-describedby.
isInvalid sets aria-invalid for validation errors.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Hides the label visually but keeps it as the name.

props.name: ...props
props.description: Native input attributes like checked and onChange.

combobox.description: A text input that filters a list of options as people type.
whenToUse: Use when there are many options and people know what they are looking for.
Use for search-style pickers like choosing an icon or a person.
whenNotToUse: For fewer than about ten options, a Select is quicker to scan.
accessibility: Follows the ARIA combobox pattern with aria-activedescendant.
The number of results is announced through a live region when nothing matches.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

input.description: A single-line text field with a built-in label, hint and error message.
whenToUse: Use for short free-form values like names, emails or search terms.
Pick the matching type, like email or password, for the right keyboard and autofill.
Use hint for format guidance and error for what went wrong and how to fix it.
whenNotToUse: Use Textarea for multi-line text.
Do not rely on the placeholder as the label; it disappears while typing.
accessibility: The label is always present; isLabelHidden only hides it visually.
Hint and error are linked with aria-describedby and the error sets aria-invalid.
Required fields are announced with a visually hidden “required”.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message. Marks the field invalid.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Content inside the end of the field, like a small button.

radio-group.description: Lets people pick exactly one option from a short list.
whenToUse: Use for two to six mutually exclusive options that should all be visible.
Preselect a sensible default when there is one.
whenNotToUse: Use Select for long lists.
Use Checkbox when several options can be chosen.
accessibility: Renders a fieldset with a legend, so the group label is announced.
Native radios give arrow-key navigation for free.

keyboard.description: Moves to and selects the next or previous option.
Moves focus into and out of the group.

props.name: label
props.description: Group label rendered as the legend.

props.name: options
props.description: Options with value, label, hint and isDisabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

select.description: Lets people choose one value from a list in a compact dropdown.
whenToUse: Use for choosing one value from a list of roughly five to twenty options.
Give it a placeholder that tells people what to choose.
whenNotToUse: For very long lists, use Combobox so people can filter.
For two or three options, a RadioGroup shows every choice at once.
accessibility: Follows the ARIA select-only combobox pattern.
Typing characters jumps to the first matching option.
Hint and error are linked to the trigger like other fields.

keyboard.description: Opens the list or selects the active option.
Moves to the first or last option.
Closes the list without changing the value.
Jumps to the option that starts with the typed letters.

props.name: options
props.description: Options with value, label and isDisabled.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown when nothing is selected.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message. Marks the field invalid.

props.name: name
props.description: Name used when submitting a form.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

switch.description: Turns a setting on or off with an immediate effect.
whenToUse: Use for settings that apply right away, like enabling notifications.
Write the label as the setting, not as an action.
whenNotToUse: Inside a form that needs a submit step, use Checkbox instead.
accessibility: A native checkbox with role="switch", so it announces on and off.
The label is part of the clickable area.

props.name: labelPosition
props.description: Puts the label before or after the switch.

props.name: ...props
props.description: Native input attributes like checked and onChange.

textarea.description: A multi-line text field for longer free-form input.
whenToUse: Use for comments, descriptions and notes.
Set rows to hint at the expected length.
whenNotToUse: Use Input for single-line values.
accessibility: Shares the Field wrapper with Input, so label, hint and error behave the same.
People can resize it vertically.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message. Marks the field invalid.

accordion.description: A stack of headings that each reveal a section of content.
whenToUse: Use to shorten long pages such as FAQs or settings groups.
Use isExclusive when only one section should be open at a time.
whenNotToUse: Do not hide content people need to compare side by side.
accessibility: Built on native details and summary elements.
Each summary is a single tab stop with its open state announced.

keyboard.description: Opens or closes the focused section.

props.name: items
props.description: Sections with id, title, content and isOpenByDefault.

props.name: isExclusive
props.description: Closes other sections when one opens.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

avatar.description: Represents a person or entity with an image or their initials.
whenToUse: Use next to names in lists, comments and headers.
Use status to show presence.
whenNotToUse: Do not use avatars for decorative imagery; use an image instead.
accessibility: Exposes the name as the accessible label.
Falls back to initials when the image fails to load.

props.name: name
props.description: Name used for initials and the accessible label.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

badge.description: A small label for status, categories or counts.
whenToUse: Use subtle badges for status and metadata.
Use count with max to show unread numbers.
whenNotToUse: Do not make badges interactive; use Tag or Button.
Avoid more than one solid badge in the same row.
accessibility: Badges are plain text, so their content is read as is.
Pair tone with a word or icon; color alone does not carry meaning.

props.name: count
props.description: Number to show instead of children.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

card.description: A container that groups related content and actions.
whenToUse: Use to group content that belongs together, like a summary or a list item.
Use CardHeader, CardBody and CardFooter for consistent spacing.
whenNotToUse: Avoid nesting cards inside cards.
accessibility: Pick a semantic element with as, like article or li, when it fits the content.

heading.description: Titles that give a page its structure, with size independent from level.
whenToUse: Use one level 1 heading per page.
Choose level by document structure, then size by visual weight.
whenNotToUse: Do not use headings just to make text bold; use Text with weight.
accessibility: Screen reader users navigate by heading level, so keep the outline logical.
Each level has a default size, so most headings need no size prop.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size. Defaults to the size of the level.

icon.description: Over 300 hand-drawn stroke icons in 15 categories. They share one grid and stroke, and inherit the current text color.
whenToUse: Use icons to support a label, not to replace it.
Search the set below and click an icon to copy its code.
Add new icons to the matching file in components/icon/icons on the 24px grid with a 2px stroke and round caps.
whenNotToUse: Do not import an icon library.
accessibility: Icons are hidden from assistive technology unless you pass label.
Pass label only when the icon carries meaning that is not written next to it.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name. Makes the icon meaningful.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

kbd.description: Shows a keyboard key or shortcut.
whenToUse: Use in help text, tooltips and menus to teach shortcuts.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for code; use a code element.
accessibility: Renders a native kbd element.

skeleton.description: A placeholder that hints at the shape of content while it loads.
whenToUse: Use for content that loads in under a few seconds and has a predictable layout.
Match the real layout so nothing jumps when content arrives.
whenNotToUse: For actions or unknown layouts, use Spinner instead.
accessibility: Skeletons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
Announce loading on the surrounding region, for example with aria-busy.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

tag.description: A compact label for filters, keywords or selections that people can remove.
whenToUse: Use for selected filters or chosen values that people can remove.
whenNotToUse: For read-only status, use Badge.
accessibility: The remove button is labelled “Remove” followed by the tag label.

keyboard.description: Removes the tag when the remove button is focused.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Shows a remove button when set.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

text.description: Body copy with consistent size, weight and color.
whenToUse: Use for paragraphs, labels and inline emphasis.
Use the muted tone for secondary details like timestamps.
whenNotToUse: Do not use Text for titles; use Heading.
accessibility: Truncated text keeps its full value in the DOM, so screen readers read all of it.
Status tones meet contrast on every surface.

props.name: isTruncated
props.description: Cuts off overflow with an ellipsis.

alert.description: A prominent message about the state of a page or a task.
whenToUse: Use info for neutral context, success to confirm, warning for risk and danger for errors.
Keep the title short and say what to do next in the body.
whenNotToUse: For short-lived feedback after an action, use Toast.
accessibility: Use role="alert" only for urgent messages; it interrupts screen readers.
Each tone has its own icon, so meaning is not carried by color alone.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a dismiss button when set.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

empty-state.description: Fills an area that has no content yet and points to the next step.
whenToUse: Use for empty lists, empty search results and first-run screens.
Offer one clear action that fills the space.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for errors that need attention; use Alert.
accessibility: Set headingLevel to fit the outline of the surrounding page.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

progress.description: Shows how far along a task is.
whenToUse: Use a value when progress can be measured, like uploads.
Leave value out for an indeterminate bar when the duration is unknown.
whenNotToUse: For quick waits, a Spinner is less distracting.
accessibility: Uses role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow and aria-valuemax.
The label names the task, even when it is visually hidden.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. Leave out for indeterminate.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

spinner.description: An animated indicator for short, indeterminate waits.
whenToUse: Use inside buttons and small areas while something loads.
whenNotToUse: For page-level loading with a known layout, use Skeleton.
accessibility: Announces its label through role="status".
Set isDecorative when another element already announces loading.
The animation slows down for people who prefer reduced motion.

props.name: isDecorative
props.description: Hides the spinner from assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

toast.description: A brief, non-blocking message that confirms the result of an action.
whenToUse: Use to confirm an action, like “Changes saved”.
Keep it to one short sentence.
whenNotToUse: Do not put the only copy of important information in a toast.
Do not use for errors that block the task; show them inline.
accessibility: Toasts are announced through a live region; danger toasts use role="alert".
The timer pauses while the toast is hovered or focused.
Every toast has a dismiss button.

props.name: duration
props.description: Time on screen in ms; null keeps it open.

breadcrumb.description: Shows where the current page sits in the hierarchy.
whenToUse: Use in deep hierarchies so people can jump back up.
whenNotToUse: Do not use on top-level pages or as the main navigation.
accessibility: Rendered as a nav landmark with an ordered list.
The last item is marked with aria-current="page".

props.name: items
props.description: Items with label and to; the last one is the current page.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

pagination.description: Moves between pages of a long list.
whenToUse: Use for lists where people need to reach a specific page.
whenNotToUse: For feeds people browse casually, load more content instead.
accessibility: Rendered as a nav landmark; the current page has aria-current="page".
Previous and next buttons have descriptive labels.

props.name: siblingCount
props.description: Pages shown on each side of the current one.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

tabs.description: Switches between related panels of content in the same place.
whenToUse: Use for peer sections of the same object, like Overview and Settings.
Use the pill variant as a compact segmented control.
whenNotToUse: Do not use tabs for steps in a sequence.
Avoid tabs when people need to compare panels side by side.
accessibility: Implements the ARIA tabs pattern with roving tabindex.
Only the selected tab is in the tab order; arrow keys move between tabs.

keyboard.description: Selects the previous or next tab.
Selects the first or last tab.
Moves focus into the active panel.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the tab list.

props.name: items
props.description: Tabs with id, label, content and isDisabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

dialog.description: A modal window that focuses attention on one task or decision.
whenToUse: Use to confirm destructive actions or collect a few inputs without leaving the page.
Put the primary action last in the footer.
whenNotToUse: Do not use dialogs for long forms or multi-step flows.
Do not open a dialog from another dialog.
accessibility: Built on the native dialog element, so focus is trapped and the page behind is inert.
Labelled by its title and described by its description.
Focus returns to the element that opened it.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called on Escape, backdrop click or the close button.

props.name: description
props.description: Short supporting text under the title.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

tooltip.description: A short hint that appears when a control is hovered or focused.
whenToUse: Use to name icon-only buttons or add a brief hint.
whenNotToUse: Do not put essential information or interactive content in a tooltip.
Do not add a tooltip that repeats the visible label.
accessibility: Linked to its trigger with aria-describedby.
Shows on focus as well as hover, and hides with Escape.
Stays open while the pointer is over it, as WCAG 1.4.13 requires.

props.name: placement
props.description: Side and alignment; flips when there is no room.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

container.description: Centers page content and caps its width.
whenToUse: Wrap page content so it lines up with the header.
whenNotToUse: Do not nest containers.
accessibility: Use as="main" for the main content area.

divider.description: A thin line that separates content.
whenToUse: Use to separate groups of content that spacing alone cannot.
whenNotToUse: Prefer whitespace; too many dividers make a page noisy.
accessibility: Decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology.
Set isDecorative to false for a semantic separator.

props.name: label
props.description: Text in the middle of a horizontal divider.

props.name: isDecorative
props.description: Hides the divider from assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

stack.description: Lays out children in a row or column with consistent gaps.
whenToUse: Use for one-dimensional layouts instead of writing flexbox by hand.
whenNotToUse: Use CSS grid for two-dimensional layouts.
accessibility: Pick a semantic element with as, like ul or nav, when it fits.

theme-toggle.description: A compact menu button for switching between the system, light and dark themes.
whenToUse: Place it once in the app header or in settings.
Keep System as the default so the app follows the device.
whenNotToUse: Do not show it more than once on a screen.
Do not replace it with a two-state switch; people need a way back to System.
accessibility: A menu button with aria-haspopup; the options are menuitemradio items with aria-checked.
The trigger shows the theme in use, and its accessible name is always “Theme”.
The choice is saved and applied before the first paint, so there is no flash.

keyboard.description: Opens the menu on the current theme.
Closes the menu and focuses the trigger.

copy-button.description: Copies a value to the clipboard and confirms it.
whenToUse: Use next to codes, links or IDs people often paste elsewhere.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for long passages people may want to read or select in part.
accessibility: Icon-only buttons still have a name, defaulting to “Copy”.
A polite live region announces when the value is copied.

props.name: isLabelShown
props.description: Shows the label next to the icon.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

toggle-button.description: A button that stays pressed or unpressed, like a favorite or a formatting option.
whenToUse: Use for an on/off option that takes effect immediately and lives in a toolbar.
whenNotToUse: For settings in a form, use Switch or Checkbox.
Do not change the label when pressed; the pressed state already says it.
accessibility: Exposes its state with aria-pressed.
Icon-only toggles require an aria-label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon, or the only content with aria-label.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

toggle-group.description: A set of toggle buttons where one or several can be pressed.
whenToUse: Use for related formatting or filter options shown side by side.
whenNotToUse: When exactly one option must always be chosen, use SegmentedControl.
accessibility: Grouped and labelled with role="group".
The group is a single tab stop; arrow keys move between buttons.

keyboard.description: Moves to the first or last button.

props.name: items
props.description: Buttons with value, label, icon, isLabelHidden and isDisabled.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

segmented-control.description: Switches between a few mutually exclusive views or modes.
whenToUse: Use for two to five short options that change what is shown right away.
whenNotToUse: To switch panels of content, use Tabs.
For a choice inside a form that is submitted later, use RadioGroup.
accessibility: Follows the radio group pattern with roving focus.
Icon-only options keep their label as the accessible name.

keyboard.description: Selects the previous or next option.
Selects the first or last option.

props.name: options
props.description: Options with value, label, icon, isLabelHidden and isDisabled.

props.name: isFullWidth
props.description: Stretches options to fill the row.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

checkbox-group.description: A labelled group of checkboxes for choosing several options.
whenToUse: Use when people can pick any number of options from a short list.
whenNotToUse: For a single yes/no choice, use one Checkbox.
For long lists, use a multi-select or TagInput.
accessibility: Built on Fieldset, so the legend names the group.
The group hint and error describe the whole group.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name shared by the checkboxes.

props.name: options
props.description: Options with value, label, hint and isDisabled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the checked values in option order.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

fieldset.description: Groups related form controls under one legend.
whenToUse: Use for parts of a form that belong together, like an address.
whenNotToUse: Do not wrap a single control in a fieldset; use its own label.
accessibility: Uses the native fieldset and legend elements.
Hint and error are linked with aria-describedby.
isDisabled disables every control inside at once.

props.name: isLegendHidden
props.description: Hides the legend visually but keeps it for screen readers.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

form.description: Connects react-hook-form to the design system fields, with validation and a submit button.
whenToUse: Use for any form with validation; pair it with a zod schema and zodResolver.
Render each control through FormField so its error shows on the field.
whenNotToUse: For a single search box or filter that submits on change, a plain input is enough.
accessibility: Native validation is turned off so messages are consistent and announced through the field.
react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field on submit.
FormSubmit shows a busy state while the form submits.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

number-input.description: A text field for numbers with step buttons, limits and locale formatting.
whenToUse: Use for quantities and amounts that people adjust in small steps.
whenNotToUse: For values like phone or card numbers, use Input; they are not quantities.
For an approximate value on a scale, use Slider.
accessibility: Exposed as a spin button with its value, minimum and maximum.
The step buttons are skipped by Tab because the arrow keys do the same.
Typed values are checked and clamped when the field loses focus.

keyboard.description: Steps the value; hold Shift for ten steps.
Jumps to the minimum or maximum.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

password-input.description: A password field with a button to show or hide what was typed.
whenToUse: Use for every password field, so people can check what they typed.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for one-time codes; use PinInput.
accessibility: The reveal button is a toggle with aria-pressed and a clear name.
Autocomplete defaults to current-password; use new-password on sign-up forms.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

search-input.description: A search field with an icon and a button to clear it.
whenToUse: Use to filter a list or search a section of the app.
whenNotToUse: For picking one option from a known list, use Combobox.
accessibility: Uses type="search", so it is announced as a search box.
The clear button appears only when there is text and returns focus to the field.

props.name: onSearch
props.description: Called on Enter or when cleared.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

pin-input.description: A row of single-character cells for verification codes.
whenToUse: Use for short one-time codes sent by email or SMS.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for passwords or long codes; use PasswordInput or Input.
accessibility: Each cell is labelled with its position, and the group has a legend.
The first cell uses one-time-code autocomplete, so phones can fill it in.
Pasting a code fills every cell.

keyboard.description: Fills the cell and moves to the next one.
Clears the cell, or the previous one when empty.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Called when every cell is filled.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names merged onto the root element.

slider.description: Picks a value, or a range with RangeSlider, by dragging along a track.
whenToUse: Use for approximate values where the relative position matters more than the exact number.
whenNotToUse: When people need an exact value, use NumberInput.
accessibility: Built on native range inputs, so every assistive technology supports it.
formatValue also sets aria-valuetext, so units are announced.
Each RangeSlider thumb has its own label.

keyboard.description: Moves to the minimum or maximum.

file-upload.description: Picks files with a button or by dropping them, and lists what was chosen.
whenToUse: Use for attachments, imports and profile photos.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it to upload many files in the background; show progress for each file instead.
accessibility: The browse button is the keyboard path; dropping is an extra for pointer users.
Each chosen file has a remove button that names the file.
Files that do not match accept are ignored.

tag-input.description: A field where people type values and turn them into removable tags.
whenToUse: Use for free-form lists like keywords, labels or email recipients.
whenNotToUse: When every value must come from a fixed list, use CheckboxGroup or Combobox.
accessibility: Instructions for adding and removing tags are linked to the field.

calendar.description: A month grid for picking a date or a range of dates.
whenToUse: Use inline when the calendar is the main content, like booking a slot.
whenNotToUse: Inside a form, use DatePicker so the calendar only shows when needed.
accessibility: Follows the ARIA date grid pattern with one tab stop.
Every day is named with its full date, and today is marked with aria-current.
Month and weekday names come from the current language.
The month title opens month and year grids, so people can jump far without paging.

keyboard.description: Moves to the start or end of the week.
Moves by one month; hold Shift for a year.

date-picker.description: A date field people can type into or fill from a calendar. DateRangePicker does the same for a range, and DateTimePicker adds a time.
whenToUse: Use for dates in forms, like due dates, bookings or report periods.
Give DateRangePicker presets for the ranges people pick most.
whenNotToUse: For a date that is always far in the past, like a birthday, typing is enough; turn off the Today button.
For a calendar that is the main content of the page, use Calendar.
accessibility: The field accepts typed dates in the order of the current language, with any separator, and shows the pattern as a placeholder.
Dates that are not real or not allowed are explained in the field error and never reach onChange.
The calendar opens in a popover with focus on the selected day and returns focus to the field after a choice.
Each range field is named after the label, so screen readers hear which end they are editing.
DateTimePicker keeps the chosen time when a new day is picked, and names its time field after the label.

keyboard.description: Moves the calendar by a month; hold Shift for a year.
In the DateTimePicker time field, moves by timeStep.

rating.description: Shows or collects a star rating.

whenNotToUse: Do not use stars for precise scores; show the number instead.

The read-only rating is one image with a text equivalent like “4 out of 5”.

avatar-group.description: A stack of overlapping avatars with a count for the rest.
whenToUse: Use to show who is in a team, a thread or a shared document.
whenNotToUse: When people need to read every name, use a list.
accessibility: A labelled list; each avatar is named after its person.

code-block.description: Shows highlighted code with a copy button.
whenToUse: Use for snippets people read or copy, like API keys or setup steps.
whenNotToUse: For a short value inside a sentence, use an inline code element.
accessibility: The code is a focusable, labelled group, so keyboard users can scroll it.
Long code collapses behind a button that reports aria-expanded.

description-list.description: Pairs of terms and values, like the details of an order.

props.name: className

stat.description: A key number with its label and change over time.

whenNotToUse: For trends over many periods, use a chart.

whenNotToUse: For a single record, use DescriptionList.
On narrow screens with few columns, a list of cards may read better.

Sortable headers are buttons and report aria-sort.
Row checkboxes have names, and the header checkbox shows a mixed state.
